Optimal.Notes: A 30 fps cap at 40 Hz refresh gives a smooth, tear-free experience for questing and exploration; expect dips to 25 fps during world boss fights or node wars. Bumping textures and character quality to Medium keeps the game looking reasonable without a large GPU cost.

profiles.Summary: Black Desert is a demanding open-world MMORPG that runs on the Steam Deck via Proton with a gold/trending-platinum rating, though it is officially Unsupported; expect playable but not polished performance. The game's recommended GPU (GTX 1660 Super) exceeds the Deck's capability, so low settings with FSR upscaling are necessary to stay near 30 fps in busy areas.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements vs. Deck GPU capability and the gold/trending-platinum ProtonDB tier. On first launch, verify the Pearl Abyss launcher loads correctly with GE-Proton, then check frame rates in a populated town — if performance is worse than expected, drop to the Max Battery profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: Use Black Desert's built-in 'Optimization Mode' preset if available to apply low settings globally. Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 significantly reduces GPU load for open-world exploration and questing.

KnownIssues: Officially 'Unsupported' by Valve — may require manual Proton selection and launcher workarounds to launch
The Pearl Abyss launcher can cause launch failures; players may need to set Proton version manually or use launch options to bypass it
Online MMORPG requires a stable internet connection; performance can dip heavily in crowded areas (node wars, world bosses)

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full native resolution with no TDP limit pushes the Deck as hard as it can go; 40 fps is achievable in open fields and towns but will drop noticeably in large-scale PvP or world boss encounters. Monitor thermals — the Deck will run hot at sustained 15 W.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap deliver a smooth, judder-free feel that suits MMO pacing well. FSR upscaling from 1024x640 recovers sharpness lost from the lower render resolution while keeping the GPU within budget.

profiles.Summary: Black Desert is a demanding open-world MMORPG whose recommended GPU (GTX 1660 Super) exceeds the Steam Deck's capability, making low settings and FSR upscaling necessary to maintain a playable 30 fps in most areas. ProtonDB reporters trend platinum with GE-Proton, so the game is broadly playable despite Valve's Unsupported rating, though busy areas like node wars and world bosses will cause notable frame drops.

On first run, check frame rate in a populated town or during combat and drop to the Optimal or MaxBattery profile if performance is unstable.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 and upscaling with FSR keeps GPU load low enough to sustain the 8 W TDP cap. Expect dips below 30 fps during large group events — this profile prioritises battery life over visual quality.

KnownIssues: Steam Deck Verified status is 'Unsupported' — controller mapping and UI navigation may require workarounds.
Only partial controller support; some menus and the in-game keyboard may require touchscreen or mouse input.
Densely populated areas (node wars, large world bosses) can cause significant frame drops well below the open-world baseline.
The game requires a persistent internet connection and Pearl Abyss account login, which can add friction under Proton at first launch.

MaxPerformance.Notes: This profile pushes the Deck's APU to its limit — the fan will run loudly and battery life is short. Drop shadow quality to Low or rendering distance to Low if frame rate dips below 40 fps in busy zones.
